dataset: Swiss Dwellings v3.0.0 (Archilyse AG), https://zenodo.org/records/7788422, CC BY 4.0. Only aggregate results are stored here.
procedure: scripts/swiss_calibrate.py (pre-registered in its docstring): real rule functions r_room_min_area / r_room_min_width on residential apartments rotated to their dominant wall direction; gate >= 90 % quiet; seeded defects (bedroom 7.0 m2, living room 2.0 m across) must be caught.

runs.run: double: 300 apartments with >= 2 bedrooms, largest = principal double (pre-registered, scripts/swiss_stack_calibrate.py)
stack: 300 consecutive-floor pairs with different plans (pre-registered)
runs.verdict: FAILED (48.0 % quiet; 52.3 % counting kitchens). Diagnosis of the 713 unstacked upper bathrooms: 276 have no overlap with a lower wet room, about 293 sit within 1.5 m (short horizontal runs), only 29 use a shaft continuous from below. Real buildings with differing floors do not consistently stack; the check is not a quality criterion and was not tuned.

flag_causes: genuinely small rooms (about 2.03 m wide, 7.2 m2): below the single-bedroom minimum
open-plan dining ZONES labelled as separate areas (4.7-5.4 m2): the rule judges a zone as a room - known limit, not amended post hoc

margins.note: thresholds sit just below the real 1st percentile: they bite in the tail, they are not vacuous

limits: wet_stack is a BRIEF check (the pilot proposes stacking), not a calibrated quality criterion: about half of real differing-floor pairs do not stack
the 'other double bedroom' 2.55 m width is not tested (which further bedrooms are doubles is unknown)

area_match, gross_area, circulation_area, within_plot, upper_supported, living_north, links_built compare a design with its own brief or plot: arithmetic, covered by unit tests (tests/test_concept.py), not by real plans

status.AREA-01 / DIM-01 principal double (11.5: calibrated on real plans (98.7 % / 97.7 % quiet, 300/300 seeded)
status.wet_stack: not a quality criterion (real-plan run failed, 48 %); kept as a brief-compliance check
